raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through like I do every year before the season really gets going.

---

I'm getting up there — 56 now, been at this 30 years. My 9.5 mu isn't much, but with seven mouths at home and a couple of the kids working in town, we get by. The off-farm money is what keeps us steady; the land mostly feeds us and covers itself if I'm careful. I can't afford to waste fertilizer or water, but I also can't afford a bad harvest.

**Wheat (the winter crop).** I'll plant around October 10-12, same as always, after I clear the maize stubble. I use Jimai variety — the seed shop stocks it, neighbors around here all grow it, does fine on our soil. About 12 kg of seed per mu, maybe a bit more since October planting can be cool. For fertilizer, I put down a compound base (diammonium phosphate, about 25 kg/mu) before planting — that's my P and some N. Then I topdress urea at green-up in early March, around 15 kg/mu. The extension agent last year said I could cut the N a bit, but I don't want to risk it — yellow wheat at jointing is the worst feeling. So total N comes out around 16-17 kg/mu.

Irrigation — I'll water three times if the winter is dry: once before winter to settle the roots, once at green-up with the topdressing, once at jointing. If it rains decent in May I skip the grain-filling irrigation. Pumping costs are real — 30-40 yuan per mu each round. Yield I'm hoping for 420-450 kg/mu. Last year I got 430, conditions looked similar.

Pesticide: I'll spray herbicide in spring for broadleaf weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll do one insecticide pass. No fungicide unless something obvious shows up.

**Maize (summer crop).** This is the tight one. Wheat combine leaves the field around June 10-12, and I need maize in the ground within the week or I lose degree-days. I do no-till with a hired planter — pay about 30 yuan/mu for the service, it's worth it. Zhengdan hybrid seed, about 2 kg/mu at around 40 yuan/mu for the seed.

Fertilizer: I put compound fertilizer down with the seed (about 25 kg/mu of NPK compound), then topdress urea at the big-flare stage in late July, maybe 15 kg/mu. Total N works out to about 16 kg/mu. Irrigation once or twice depending on July-August rain — usually we get enough but if it's dry at silking I pump. Pesticide: one spray for corn borer at whorl stage is standard here. Yield target 480-500 kg/mu.

**Labor and costs.** Most of this is me and my wife. My older son comes back from town for wheat harvest and maize planting — that crunch week. Otherwise I handle it. I hire the combine (wheat and maize) and the planter. Total input cost for both crops, I'd guess around 7,000-7,500 yuan across the 9.5 mu.
